clue.text: Embarrassed by pretence adopted by a newspaperman

indicators.note: something adopted by a pair is taken in among them, so the pretence goes inside

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, a newspaperman
a sham is a pretence or fake show

explanation.surface: A journalist is shamed by being caught up in a pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; 'adopted by' is the container signal, so the pretence sits inside the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe feeling mortified and self-conscious over something.

clue.text: Place in Hampshire with some cricket

parts.note: and joins things, like with
an over is a set of six balls, a portion of a cricket match

explanation.surface: A Hampshire town known for its local cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled by one bowler. Andover is a town in Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a market town in the county of Hampshire, England.

clue.text: Parliament whips roof off church

parts.note: the House is a chamber of Parliament

indicators.note: off here means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Parliamentary row in which party whips strip the roof off a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whips' looks like party whips in Parliament, but it is only anagram fodder with 'roof'.
explanation.definitionFit: A church is one kind of building used for religious services.

clue.text: Married to drink? He certainly is

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A husband wedded to his beer, who is certainly a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: 'He' is certainly of this sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun 'he' refers to a man, so he is certainly of masculine gender.

clue.text: Get rid of diamonds, one spade and joker

parts.note: D abbreviates diamonds, a card suit
I is the Roman numeral one
S abbreviates spades, a card suit
a joker is a card, and also a card is a joker or wag

explanation.surface: A card player throws away a diamond, a spade and the joker.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to throw out or dispose of something unwanted.

clue.text: A kick in the shins from a horse

explanation.surface: Someone gets kicked in the shins by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking is kicking an opponent's shins in football; a hack is also a riding horse for hire.

clue.text: Manage to prevent execution?

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop an execution taking place.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a beheading: the head comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercept or forestall is the first sense; beheading takes the head off, the second.

clue.text: Morse's enigma

explanation.surface: The puzzle that faced Inspector Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse's system of dots and dashes is a code; an enigma is a puzzle or cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code is a signalling system; an enigma or cipher is a secret writing system.

clue.text: One who gives cover with hesitation, after fixing ruins

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound behind the rearranged letters
fixing suggests repairing or rearranging, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant insurance company finally pays out to repair ruined property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'after' fixes the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriting company provides insurance cover against loss.

clue.text: Act with time to study article on directors

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
the is the definite article
a company's board is its directors

explanation.surface: Instructions for an actor: take time to study a piece about company directors.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform on stage as an actor, the stage boards being trodden.

clue.text: Twice as many flags? They're not ethically right

explanation.surface: Doubling the number of flags flown is not a moral thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard is a flag, so twice as many are double standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying different moral rules to different people is hypocrisy; doubled banners are the cryptic sense.

clue.text: The sight of centre-forward following struggle

indicators.note: following places the middle letter behind the word for struggle

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word forward

explanation.surface: A football match where we watch the centre-forward battling for the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is something seen, a scene or prospect.

clue.text: Love found aboard bamboo craft

indicators.note: being found aboard means sitting inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bamboo stems are cane
love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms on a raft made of bamboo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found aboard' puts O inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light boat, one kind of watercraft.

clue.text: The food is rumoured to be okay

indicators.note: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so this word is heard, not read

parts.note: fare is food, as on a menu

explanation.surface: Gossip says the food here is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rumoured' signals that FARE is heard as its twin in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means reasonable or acceptable, as in a fair result.

clue.text: Water rates of the windsors, perhaps

explanation.surface: The royal family paying their water bills.
explanation.walkthrough: A knot is a nautical mile per hour, a speed at sea; a Windsor is a style of tie knot, so the lower case 'windsors' are not the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeds on water are measured in nautical units; a Windsor is a kind of necktie tie.

clue.text: Complains about vehicles parking inside

indicators.note: inside means the parking letter sits within the vehicles

parts.note: cars are vehicles
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about cars parked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to grumble or find fault.

clue.text: Penalised once more for being elegant?

explanation.surface: Is a second fine a mark of sophistication?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as RE-FINED, fined again.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined means cultured and polished; re-fined is fined again.

clue.text: More deflated by praise

explanation.surface: Someone feels lower after being praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatter is the comparative of flat, less puffed up; to flatter is to compliment insincerely.

clue.text: Head of state looked sulky — and gushed

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of state

parts.note: to pout is to look sulky

explanation.surface: A head of state pouted and then poured out words.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouted means poured out in a stream, as a whale or fountain does.

clue.text: Mature, in ways, getting insignia of promotion

indicators.note: in places the word for mature inside the ways

parts.note: ST abbreviates street, a way, so ways are STS
ripe means mature

explanation.surface: Someone matures in their ways and earns promotion badges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word; ST, short for street, made plural stands for ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes on a uniform sleeve show rank, gained by promotion.

clue.text: Germany is eager for scraps

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
someone who itches to do something is eager

explanation.surface: Germany keen to get into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' looks like fights, but here it is the verb: throws away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to abandon or throw away, as one scraps a plan.

clue.text: Meals for those who drink

explanation.surface: Evening meals for drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: To sup is to drink, so suppers are those who sip.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal; one who sups takes liquid by mouthfuls.

clue.text: Withdraw from contest through minor injury

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls out of a race because of a small injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratching a runner removes it from a race; a scratch is a slight wound.

clue.text: Substitute with status finally disappearing

indicators.note: finally disappearing tells us the last letter of the word for status vanishes

parts.note: standing means status or rank

explanation.surface: A replacement whose position is fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally disappearing' removes the last letter, G, from STANDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a replacement who takes another's place.

clue.text: The trick is to get employment by right

indicators.note: by means next to, so the right letter stands beside the word for employment

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: The secret of getting a job is to be on the right side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a cunning stratagem meant to deceive.

clue.text: Austere mariner in case of shock

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the outside of shock
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A stern sailor in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' here means the outer shell of the word shock, not a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means bare and severe, without ornament.

clue.text: A month with a star!

parts.note: Nov abbreviates November, a month

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a month spent with a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly brightens hugely.

clue.text: Prison unrest

explanation.surface: Riots breaking out in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: STIR is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail; a stir is also a commotion.

clue.text: Thinking primarily of victory in match

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter of Thinking

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Focusing chiefly on winning the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game, but here it means a counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is something that matches another exactly, a pair or double.

clue.text: Celebrate thirteen down — apt after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some rough way, so the letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to celebrate the entry at thirteen down, apparently fittingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thirteen down' looks like a reference to 13-down, but is just anagram fodder with APT, rearranged as 'after a fashion' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out and party lavishly is an idiom for celebrating.

clue.text: A sailor bearing weapons

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine, a seagoing serviceman
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: RM (Royal Marine) is a crossword staple for a sailor; 'bearing' gives a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, as in firearms.

clue.text: Writing to offspring offering practical experience

parts.note: one's hand is one's handwriting
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A letter to a child that gives practical advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands-on describes direct, practical involvement rather than theory.
